name: Northern Cardinal
fact: Unlike most North American songbirds, female Northern Cardinals sing too, often while sitting on the nest. And both males and females will attack their own reflection in a window or car mirror, sometimes for hours, mostly in spring when they're defending territory.
question: Why does a cardinal keep pecking at your window?
answer: It thinks its reflection is a rival invading its territory.

name: Arctic Tern
fact: Arctic Terns migrate from pole to pole, and birds from North America travel around 25,000 miles (40,000 km) a year. They can live for decades: the oldest on record was at least 34 years old.
question: About how far does a North American Arctic Tern fly in a year?
answer: Around 25,000 miles (40,000 km), from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back.

name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
fact: A Ruby-throated Hummingbird beats its wings about 53 times a second. Its legs are so short it can't walk or hop; the best it can do is shuffle along a perch.
question: Guess: how many times a second do its wings beat?

name: Peregrine Falcon
fact: In its hunting dive (a stoop) from more than 1 km up, a Peregrine Falcon may reach 320 km/h (200 mph). Even chasing prey in level flight it can hit about 112 km/h (69 mph).
question: How fast can a diving Peregrine Falcon go?

name: Common Raven
fact: Common Ravens are aerial acrobats: one was seen flying upside down for more than half a mile. Raised in captivity they can even imitate human words, and one was taught to say "nevermore."
question: Can a raven learn to talk?
answer: Yes. In captivity ravens can imitate human words; one learned to say "nevermore."

name: Atlantic Puffin
fact: Puffin chicks are called "pufflings." Puffins are long-lived too: the oldest on record was banded as a chick in Norway and lived to be 41.
question: What's a baby puffin called?

name: Great Horned Owl
fact: A Great Horned Owl's clenched talons take a force of 28 pounds to pry open. No wonder crows mob these owls for hours: the Great Horned Owl is the crow's most dangerous predator.
question: How hard is it to open a Great Horned Owl's clenched talons?
answer: It takes about 28 pounds of force.

name: Shoebill
fact: Shoebills can stand as still as a statue for hours, then strike fast, and about 60% of their attacks end in a kill. Lungfish are a favorite, but they also take frogs, water snakes and even young crocodiles.
question: What's a Shoebill's favorite fish?

name: American Crow
fact: In winter, American Crows gather in communal roosts that range from a few hundred birds up to two million. Some roosts have formed in the same general area for well over 100 years.
question: How many crows can share one winter roost?

name: North Island Brown Kiwi
fact: North Island Brown Kiwi are flightless and nocturnal, with tiny leftover wings and no tail. The female lays a very large white egg, and only the male incubates it.
question: Which kiwi parent sits on the egg?

name: Blue Jay
fact: Blue Jays aren't actually blue. The pigment in their feathers is melanin, which is brown. The blue comes from light scattering through modified cells on the surface of the feather barbs.
question: What color is a Blue Jay's feather pigment?
answer: Not blue. The pigment is melanin, which is brown. The blue is a trick of light.

name: Wandering Albatross
fact: Wandering Albatrosses have enormous wings, spanning about 3 m (nearly 10 ft). They're in no rush to start a family: most don't breed until they're 11 to 15 years old, and then raise a chick at most once every two years.
question: How wide are its wings?

name: Wild Turkey
fact: Wild Turkeys can swim: they tuck their wings in close, spread their tails and kick. They're also one of only two domesticated birds native to the Americas, along with the Muscovy Duck.
question: Can Wild Turkeys swim?
answer: Yes, by tucking in their wings, spreading their tails and kicking.

name: Greater Roadrunner
fact: Roadrunners can kill and eat rattlesnakes, often as a team: one distracts the snake while the other pins its head. Sorry, cartoon fans: real coyotes can run 43 mph, more than twice as fast as a roadrunner.
question: Could a real coyote outrun a roadrunner?
answer: Yes. Coyotes reach about 43 mph, more than twice a roadrunner's speed.

name: Turkey Vulture
fact: Turkey Vultures find dead animals by smell and can detect odors at just a few parts per trillion, even beneath a forest canopy. Get too close and one may vomit on you as a defense. Happy Halloween!
question: What might a Turkey Vulture do if you get too close?
answer: Throw up on you. Considering what it eats, that's a powerful weapon.
